summary: Polk County Texas Forest Service lookout; 1949 survey describes a steel tower about 110 ft with glass cab; listed as gone, with its survey mark reported destroyed.

facts.design: four-legged steel structure about 110 ft tall with a glass-enclosed lookout cab
facts.status_note: Listed as gone on the Forest Fire Lookout Association's Texas list; the federal survey mark for the station is reported destroyed; no source describes what remains at the site

events.note: Coast and Geodetic Survey described the station and tower, so the tower was standing by then

evidence.supports: about 10.3 miles east of Livingston, 0.3 mile north of U.S. Highway 190
evidence.quote: LOCATED ABOUT 10.3 MILES EAST OF LIVINGSTON, 0.3 MILE NORTH OF U.S. HIGHWAY 190

evidence.supports: the Coast and Geodetic Survey described the station in 1949
evidence.quote: DESCRIBED BY COAST AND GEODETIC SURVEY 1949 (RLE)
IT IS A FOUR LEGGED STEEL STRUCTURE ABOUT 110

evidence.supports: about 110 feet tall with a glass-enclosed lookout cab on top
evidence.quote: FEET HIGH WITH A GLASS ENCLOSED LOOKOUT CAB ON THE TOP.

evidence.supports: the old community lies about eight miles east of Livingston, the county seat
evidence.quote: 8 Miles E of Livingston the county seat

evidence.supports: the federal listing reports the station's surface mark as destroyed
the Texas list records the tower as gone

sources.title: NGS Data Sheet retrieval for station BL2144 (SODA LOOKOUT TOWER 64), nonpublished listing
Soda, Texas, Polk County ghost town

resolved_conflicts.explanation: Texas Escapes places the old community about eight miles east of Livingston; the 1949 survey places the station about 10.3 miles east. These describe a community and a survey station, which may be different spots, so both figures are kept and not reconciled.

notes_for_editor: Design and height come from a 1949 survey description reproduced on the Central US Lookouts page. The NGS datasheet for BL2144 is a nonpublished listing with no full description, so the 1949 text could not be checked there. The 'surface mark reported destroyed' code refers to the survey mark, not the tower. No build date, staffing or access found. The Central US Lookouts Texas page also carries an unattributed 1930 note about two steel towers (95 and 120 ft) in Polk, Tyler, Hardin and Liberty counties; it does not name Soda, so it was not used.
